items.title: Hinton Milt — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: We grew up together so he was….Lionel met us at the railroad station

ctx.x: Yeah, he was married then. In 1933 he was married to Gladys. And Gladys… they moved to California because Gladys was an excellent seamstress and she got a job sewing for one of the great movie stars, Gloria Swanson or one of the big move stars. She had a good job. Lionel got the job out there working with Les Hiss band. We grew up together so he was….Lionel met us at the railroad station, the little group playing for us as we came into town.

items.title: Milt Hinton interviewed by Joe Williams, Majesty of the Seas, May 31, 1995
items.q: Ray Nance, Lionel Hampton. You know what was so wonderful about that it was a black community, and we didn’t all go to the same school, but we all met musically.

ctx.x: Ray Nance, Lionel Hampton. You know what was so wonderful about that it was a black community, and we didn’t all go to the same school, but we all met musically. So with bands, like, you went to some school, I went to Winifred, but we had rehearsals, and then after hours, we met, and that’s how we got to know each other. And to see all of that going on, we had Clark Smith and the Chicago Defender, the newspaper, hired Basie and Clark Smith to start a youth band, and that’s where we came in. My mother was Nat…
